spec_issues: The overview and prompt agree. The prompt adds 'don't return stored answers or exploit noise seeds' and allows dev only for 'aggregate scores'. dev.npz stores its noise_seed, so agents can and did reproduce the exact dev noise for local tracking (Fable 78SNWcr/hnWjajq), but the private run draws fresh noise, so this gives no advantage.

restore.py receives the true condition_id and sigma for every sequence, so the task is non-blind Gaussian denoising with a known prior generator. The 'unseen' private sequences are i.i.d. draws from the same simulator+encoder that agents can sample without limit, which makes this a supervised-learning and capacity problem more than a modelling problem.

The starter truncates to a rank-64 PCA basis. Simply raising the rank (to ~2048-4096) and fitting the full Gaussian prior already yields reward ~2.0 of the best 2.75; every trial found this first (Gemini Flash 4LuQaZs ships only that).
verifier_issues: The private evaluation re-runs the frozen baseline on a fresh noise draw per trial: baseline_objective ranges 0.068772-0.068858, a 0.13% spread, so scores are paired and stable.

Two trials (GPT CgZXFaG, Gemini Flash 4LuQaZs) have official rewards but empty breakdowns (4LuQaZs with ArtifactCollectionError). Their rewards fit their dev results plus the common +0.06-0.08 private offset, so they look genuine but cannot be checked.
No way to game the verifier was found: the output contract is a dense array, the noise is fresh per run, and the fixed 1 GiB / 1200 s limits were far from binding (5-55 s runtimes).
task_level.noise: Very low. Every trial's private reward is its final dev reward plus 0.05-0.08 (Fable 2.671 -> 2.747, Fable 2.653 -> 2.733, GPT m5NsTAX 2.510 -> 2.588, GPT CgZXFaG ~2.583 -> 2.660, Argon 2.486 -> 2.559 and 2.439 -> 2.515, Gemini Flash 2.232 -> 2.306 and 1.987 -> 2.040, Kimi 2.149 -> 2.208 and 2.079 -> 2.142, Grok 2.135 -> 2.195 and 2.088 -> 2.158). The dev and private orderings match exactly. The baseline varies only 0.13% across trials. The only within-noise pair is Fable's two runs (2.747 vs 2.733, a 0.4% objective difference); the cross-model gaps that decide the Elo games are 1-15% in objective, far above the ~1% sampling error the agents estimated.
task_level.epoch_rationale: The scoring is stable (fresh paired noise, 0.13% baseline drift, dev and private orderings identical), so the model ordering Fable > GPT > Argon > Gemini Flash/Kimi/Grok is not noise-driven and no scoring defect changes the winner.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: No gaming. Nobody fitted on dev, used noise seeds at test time or stored answers. Most of the measured gain is generic: replacing the rank-64 truncation with a high-rank (full-data) Gaussian/Wiener prior gives ~0.0223 NMSE (reward ~2.0) for everyone. The remaining 0.2-0.75 reward comes from learned nonlinear residual correctors (U-Nets, NAFNets, MLPs, block regressors) trained on unlimited generator data. The top four trials share one task-specific insight: the frozen encoder imprints a fixed periodic (period-4/8) phase pattern, so phase-aware pixel-unshuffled networks see stationary statistics. This is competent applied denoising (known techniques), not new research, and the narrow 2.0-2.75 band mostly reflects how much nonlinear refinement each agent added on top of the same linear core.

trials.approach: Stage 1 is a rank-2048 PCA Gaussian prior with per-mode AR(1) Kalman smoothing, fitted on train.npz plus generator data (dev NMSE ~0.0224). Stage 2 is a 0.65/0.35 ensemble of two (2+1)D U-Net residual denoisers trained on generator data with sampled noise levels. They take the noisy frames and the Gaussian posterior mean and predict a correction, with a runtime fallback. The ensemble weight was chosen on dev aggregate (flat between 0.5 and 0.8).

trials.approach: Stage 1 is a pooled-eigenbasis Gaussian smoother: conditions with the same turbulence strength share frame statistics, giving 2048 eigenvectors with per-condition AR(1) dynamics and an exact posterior mean (dev 0.02242). Stage 2 is an equal-weight ensemble of two residual (2+1)D U-Nets (15M/37M parameters) on a period-8 pixel-unshuffled 16x16x64 grid, where the encoder's fixed period-8 texture makes the statistics stationary. Both stages are trained on train.npz plus generator seeds 1001-1048.

trials.approach: The PCA rank goes from 64 to 3072, capped at the number of available frames, with a diagonal per-mode AR(1) Kalman smoother solved exactly as a tridiagonal system. A 7-layer dilated CNN (refine_state_dict inside params.pt) corrects the Kalman posterior mean from the normalised estimate, the residual and sigma/latent_std.

trials.approach: Rank-4096 PCA per D/r0 group with per-mode stationary Toeplitz temporal covariance and a per-pixel temporal complement Wiener filter, fitted on train.npz plus 1,400 generator shards (~22.5k trajectories per condition), which is close to Bayes-optimal among linear estimators (0.02235). On top sits a per-frame cross-mode MLP that corrects the top-1024 coefficients (0.02118).
